name: Halcyon Dynamics Aegis Response Full Kit
description: Warm-gold and deep-navy modular hard armor over breathable climate-adaptive fatigues, bearing Halcyon's sunrise-arc logo in gilded relief on the chest plate and helmet crest — projecting authority over menace. The helmet is a mid-profile shell with integrated crowd-analytics HUD, non-lethal deterrent emitter array, and a PR-facing body camera mounted prominently at the forehead. Load rig balances lethal and non-lethal options in equal measure, with Halcyon-branded restraint kits, medkit pouches, and a community-liaison tablet holster. Boots are climate-sealed composite with cushioned insoles rated for twelve-hour standing deployment.
functionality: Crowd analytics HUD, integrated non-lethal deterrence, mandatory body-camera recording, and climate regulation for extended public-facing deployment.
what_it_says: Halcyon sells security as a wellness product — the kit is designed to be photographed as much as deployed.
story_hooks: A Halcyon operative's body camera has been remotely wiped every shift for two weeks — someone at Halcyon doesn't want certain footage preserved.
The community-liaison tablet in the load rig contains a list of names flagged for 'preemptive contact' — none of them have committed any crime yet.
